title: US Assures India a Tariff Edge Over Rivals as Trade Deal Nears First Tranche
excerpt: American negotiators have assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing economies, Indian officials say, with the first, goods-only tranche targeted for completion by March 2027.
body:
• The United States has assured India that its exporters will receive a comparative tariff advantage over rival economies under the proposed bilateral trade deal, a senior Indian government official said on Friday.
  • The first tranche covers goods only; services will be taken up in a later tranche, and both sides aim to complete the first tranche by the end of the current financial year, in March 2027.
  • The final tariff rates are not yet fixed: they depend on the outcome of the US Trade Representative's Section 301 investigation into industrial overcapacity, covering 60 economies.
  • For Indian exporters, the edge would matter most in labour-intensive goods such as textiles, where India competes with Vietnam, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh.

The United States has assured India that its exporters will face lower tariffs than rival economies under the proposed bilateral trade agreement, a senior Indian government official said on Friday, addressing the condition New Delhi had set for moving the deal forward.

"Talks between India and the US are ongoing and the US has assured us of a comparative advantage over our competitor countries," the official said, according to reporting on the briefing. The assurance goes back to the February 2026 joint statement by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump, in which the two sides committed to preferential market access for each other.

What the first tranche covers — and what it leaves out

The first tranche of the agreement covers goods only. Services and other matters will follow in later tranches. The deal will take the form of a legal text with annexures, including a dedicated chapter on customs and trade facilitation; a two-member US team visited India on November 2-3 and resolved several portions of that chapter, officials said.

The legal text is also expected to bar Washington from imposing additional tariffs beyond what it commits to. If future US tariffs exceed those commitments, India reserves the right to modify its own concessions, the official said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal has said the negotiations are "on the right path," and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has described the outcome India has negotiated as among the best it could obtain.

The number that is not settled yet

The assurance does not yet fix the tariff rates Indian exporters will actually pay. Under the separate Section 301 forced-labour tariffs finalised on July 23, India currently pays an extra 10% on about 55% of its US-bound exports — the same rate as Indonesia, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Malaysia — while China, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines pay 12.5%, MLQ's summary of the official briefing reported.

The final structure depends on a second Section 301 investigation, into "structural excess capacity" in manufacturing, which the US Trade Representative opened in March and which covers 60 economies including India. Until that probe concludes, the size of India's advantage remains the main open variable. Indian merchandise exports to the US rose to $59.52 billion in April-October from $51.99 billion a year earlier, so the rate that finally applies will move a large and growing trade flow.

What to watch

No further in-person negotiating rounds are planned for now, a government source said, with chief negotiators in touch virtually. The target is to conclude the first tranche by March 2027. Exporters in textiles and other labour-intensive sectors — where a percentage point or two against Vietnam or Bangladesh decides orders — have the most riding on the Section 301 outcome and the rates written into the final text.
